To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the diversity of a firm’s inventive human capital, in terms of technical experience, should be organized with greater across-team than within-team diversity, as this diversity regime leads to greater firm-level innovation.
firms that have a greater degree of across-team diversity in their human capital have more stable teams and more innovative products.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the organization of human capital within a firm affects its performance, with a particular focus on firm-level innovation.

the implications of alternate organizational designs on firm-level innovation, as a function of how a firm chooses to organize its human capital, and how that organization influences the firm’s human resource stability.

the question of how to organize a firm’s human and social capital when innovation performance is a desired outcome, and our findings provide evidence that the answer to this question depends on the nature of the diversity regime in place.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a firm should organize its human capital with greater diversity across teams when it is important to the firm that its human capital remain in place for a longer time period.
the optimal organization of a firm’s human resources is one that balances within-team and across-team diversity, such that the firm is able to reap the innovation benefits of both types of diversity.
the benefits of within-team diversity are not as strong as the benefits of across team diversity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
firms should organize their human capital to achieve greater across-team diversity when firm-level innovation benefits are the desired outcome.
the optimal design of the human capital pool is a function of the firm’s ability to retain that pool.
the benefits of greater within-team diversity are outweighed by the benefits of increased firm-level stability that are associated with greater across-team human capital diversity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a diversity of experience is valuable, but it is the diversity regime that matters.
a firm-level diversity regime can influence the stability of the firm’s inventive teams and, in turn, the firm’s innovation performance.
the optimal organization of human capital within a firm depends on the specific innovation goals of the firm, as well as the specific characteristics of the human capital available to the firm.
